QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_31

question.text: What is the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund (Core SGF) and who contributes to it?

answer.text: A segment fund maintained by the clearing corporation to guarantee settlement and cover default losses, contributed to by the clearing corporation (at least 50% of MRC), the stock exchange (at least 25%), clearing members (up to 25%), plus penalties and interest accrued
A government-backed fund that guarantees all exchange trades
An insurance policy purchased by the clearing corporation
A fund maintained by SEBI to compensate retail investors

explanation.text: The Logic: The Core Settlement Guarantee Fund (Core SGF) is the segment fund used to guarantee settlement and complete the settlement on a member's default. As per the source contribution structure: the clearing corporation contributes at least 50% of the Minimum Required Corpus (MRC) from its own funds, the stock exchange contributes at least 25%, clearing members contribute up to 25%, and the balance is built up via penalties and interest. The Trap: The Core SGF is not government-backed (option B) nor an insurance product purchased by the clearing corporation (option C). It is also not maintained by SEBI for investor compensation (option D) -- that is a different mechanism. The clearing corporation maintains the Core SGF under SEBI's regulatory framework. Note: Workbook reference: NISM Series IV pp.270-273. Note especially the contribution shares (CC at least 50% of MRC, SE at least 25%, CM up to 25%, plus penalties and interest).
